title: Squeeze out the padding
description:
Every type has an alignment, and the compiler inserts invisible **padding** bytes so that each member starts at a suitable address. The order you declare members in decides how much.

`Wasteful` holds 18 bytes of real data but takes up **32**. Write a struct `Compact` with the same six members (same names, same types) in a better order, so that it takes up only **24**.

Rule of thumb: put the members with the largest alignment first.
lessonTitle: Memory Layout, Alignment, Unions and Bit Fields
